sources.entry: Applite - User-friendly GUI app for Homebrew Casks. Install, update, and uninstall apps with a single click.

summary.one_liner: Applite is a native macOS app store GUI for installing, updating, and uninstalling Homebrew Cask apps, and it bundles its own Homebrew so no Terminal or Command Line Tools are needed.
summary.what_it_does: Applite provides a graphical catalog of Homebrew Casks (macOS GUI apps) organized into categories with icons and a search field. It can install, update, and uninstall apps with one click. On first launch it downloads a Homebrew tarball into its own Application Support directory and runs it from there, or it can use an existing Homebrew prefix chosen in Settings. The cask catalog is stored in a local SQLite database synced from the Homebrew JSON API, with FTS5 full-catalog search. It also supports Brewfile import and export for migrating apps to a new Mac, custom taps, and HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS5 system proxies. Installed and outdated state is loaded from brew list and brew outdated after the UI is already shown.
use_cases: Install Mac apps without using Terminal
Update or remove Homebrew cask apps from a GUI
Migrate installed apps to a new Mac with a Brewfile
Browse and search Homebrew casks by category
Set up a fresh Mac with non-App Store software
how_to_run: Download the DMG from applite.app or the project's direct DMG link
Or install with: brew install --cask applite
Requires macOS 14 or later (universal binary, Apple Silicon and Intel)
notable: Bundles its own Homebrew, so it can be the first app on a fresh Mac
Casks only, with no formulae, services, or CLI surface
Brewfile import and export with a per-app selection sheet
Two-stage loading: SQLite paints the UI first, then brew state fills in
Localized in 7 languages, with no telemetry
caveats: Casks only, so formulae and services are not managed
Sole maintainer with limited development time; releases are periodic
Uses AI-assisted development (Claude Code) from version 1.4 onward, as stated by the author
